description: This topic introduces the meaning of computer storage, the difference between primary and secondary storage, common storage devices, units of storage and their relationships, volatile and non-volatile memory, and how to choose and care for storage media.

mcq.questionText: What does the term 'storage' mean in a computer system?

options.text: The process of holding data and instructions for later use
The process of typing text into a keyboard
The process of printing documents on paper
The process of switching the computer on and off

mcq.explanation: Storage refers to keeping data and instructions in the computer so they can be retrieved and used when needed.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of primary storage?
mcq.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is primary storage that the CPU uses directly while a program is running.

mcq.questionText: How many bits make up one byte?
mcq.explanation: One byte is made up of 8 bits, and a byte usually represents a single character.

mcq.questionText: Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is switched off?
mcq.explanation: Volatile memory, such as RAM, loses all stored data once the power is turned off.

mcq.questionText: Which storage device uses laser light to read and write data?
mcq.explanation: Optical discs such as CDs and DVDs are read and written using a laser beam.

mcq.questionText: Which storage option keeps your files on remote internet servers so you can access them from anywhere?
mcq.explanation: Cloud storage saves data on servers reached over the internet, allowing access from any connected device.

mcq.questionText: Which unit of storage is the largest among those listed below?
mcq.explanation: Among KB, MB, GB and TB, the terabyte is the largest unit of storage.

mcq.questionText: Approximately how many kilobytes are there in one megabyte?
mcq.explanation: One megabyte equals 1024 kilobytes, since each higher unit is 1024 times the previous one.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a small, portable storage device that plugs into a USB port?
mcq.explanation: A flash disk (USB flash drive) is a small portable device that connects through a USB port to store data.

mcq.questionText: Which type of storage is commonly used inside cameras and mobile phones?
mcq.explanation: Memory cards are small flash storage devices widely used in cameras and mobile phones.

mcq.questionText: Why is secondary storage needed in addition to primary storage?

options.text: Because secondary storage works faster than the CPU
Because it keeps data permanently even when the power is off
Because it replaces the need for a processor
Because it cannot store any files

mcq.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile, so it keeps data permanently for later use, unlike volatile primary memory.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes ROM?

options.text: Memory that the user can easily change all the time
Non-volatile memory that mainly stores start-up instructions
A removable storage device for photos
An optical disc read by a laser

mcq.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile and usually holds the instructions a computer needs to start up.

mcq.questionText: A student needs to store a 50 GB collection of videos for many years. Which storage is most appropriate?
mcq.explanation: An external hard disk offers large capacity and permanent storage, suitable for keeping many gigabytes of videos.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a good practice for caring for storage media?

options.text: Removing a flash disk while files are still being copied
Keeping CDs in direct sunlight for a long time
Safely ejecting a flash disk before removing it
Touching the shiny data surface of a CD with dirty fingers

mcq.explanation: Safely ejecting a device before removal prevents data loss and damage to the files and the device.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly compares primary and secondary storage?

options.text: Primary storage is usually faster but smaller than secondary storage
Secondary storage is always faster than primary storage
Primary storage keeps data permanently after power off
Secondary storage is used directly by the CPU during processing

mcq.explanation: Primary storage like RAM is faster and used directly by the CPU but has smaller capacity than secondary storage.

fib.questionText: The smallest unit of data storage in a computer is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A bit is the smallest unit of storage and holds either a 0 or a 1.

fib.questionText: One byte is made up of eight _____.
fib.explanation: Eight bits combine to form one byte, which usually represents one character.

fib.questionText: Memory that loses its contents when power is turned off is described as _____ memory.
fib.explanation: Volatile memory such as RAM needs constant power to keep its data.

fib.questionText: The type of storage that holds data permanently even without power is called _____ storage.
fib.explanation: Secondary storage, such as a hard disk, keeps data permanently for later use.

fib.questionText: A storage service that keeps files on remote internet servers is known as _____ storage.
fib.explanation: Cloud storage saves data on internet-based servers accessible from any connected device.

fib.questionText: The main internal device for storing large amounts of data permanently in a desktop computer is the _____.
fib.explanation: The hard disk is the main internal secondary storage device with large capacity.

fib.questionText: 1024 megabytes are approximately equal to one _____.
fib.explanation: One gigabyte equals 1024 megabytes in the binary system of measurement.

fib.questionText: CDs and DVDs are examples of _____ storage media because they use laser light.
fib.explanation: Optical storage media are read and written using a laser beam.

fib.questionText: The memory inside a computer that the CPU uses directly while running programs is called _____.
fib.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) temporarily holds data and programs the CPU is currently using.

fib.questionText: Choosing storage according to how much data it can hold means considering its storage _____.
fib.explanation: Storage capacity tells how much data a device can hold and helps in choosing suitable storage.

tf.questionText: RAM is an example of volatile memory.
tf.explanation: RAM loses its contents when the power is switched off, so it is volatile.

tf.questionText: A hard disk loses all its data as soon as the computer is switched off.
tf.explanation: A hard disk is non-volatile and keeps data permanently even without power.

tf.questionText: One kilobyte is larger than one megabyte.
tf.explanation: A megabyte is larger than a kilobyte; 1 MB equals 1024 KB.

tf.questionText: Cloud storage allows users to access their files over the internet from different devices.
tf.explanation: Cloud storage keeps files on internet servers that can be reached from any connected device.

tf.questionText: A bit can hold only the value 0 or the value 1.
tf.explanation: A bit is the smallest unit of storage and represents either 0 or 1.

tf.questionText: Memory cards are commonly used in cameras and mobile phones.
tf.explanation: Memory cards are small flash storage devices widely used in cameras and phones.

tf.questionText: Primary storage usually has a larger capacity than secondary storage.
tf.explanation: Secondary storage normally has much larger capacity than primary storage such as RAM.

tf.questionText: It is safe to pull out a flash disk while files are still being copied to it.
tf.explanation: Removing a flash disk during copying can corrupt files and damage data; it should be safely ejected first.

tf.questionText: ROM is a type of non-volatile memory.
tf.explanation: ROM keeps its contents even when the power is off, so it is non-volatile.

tf.questionText: A terabyte is smaller than a gigabyte.
tf.explanation: A terabyte is larger than a gigabyte; 1 TB equals 1024 GB.

summary.correctAnswer: Holding data and instructions for later use
summary.explanation: Storage keeps data and instructions so they can be retrieved when needed.

summary.correctAnswer: Fast memory used directly by the CPU, such as RAM and ROM
summary.explanation: Primary storage works closely with the CPU during processing.

summary.correctAnswer: Non-volatile storage that keeps data permanently, such as hard disks
summary.explanation: Secondary storage holds data even when the computer is off.

summary.correctAnswer: Memory that loses its data when power is off, like RAM
summary.explanation: Volatile memory needs constant power to keep its contents.

summary.correctAnswer: Memory that keeps data without power, like ROM and hard disks
summary.explanation: Non-volatile memory retains data even after switching off.

summary.correctAnswer: The bit, which holds a 0 or a 1
summary.explanation: All data is built from bits, the smallest storage unit.

summary.correctAnswer: 8 bits = 1 byte, and each unit up is 1024 times the previous
summary.explanation: KB, MB, GB and TB each increase by a factor of 1024.

summary.correctAnswer: Storing files on internet servers accessible from anywhere
summary.explanation: Cloud storage lets users reach files from any connected device.

summary.correctAnswer: Consider capacity, portability, cost and speed
summary.explanation: The right storage depends on the amount of data and how it will be used.

summary.correctAnswer: Eject safely, avoid heat and dust, and handle gently
summary.explanation: Proper care prevents data loss and damage to storage devices.

hoq.questionText: A photographer is taking pictures in a remote village with no internet for a whole week and must keep thousands of large photos until returning to town. Which storage choice is most suitable during the trip?

options.text: Cloud storage, because it can be accessed anywhere
High-capacity memory cards and a portable hard disk
The camera's RAM, because it is very fast
A single CD, because it is cheap

hoq.explanation: Without internet, cloud storage is not usable; large-capacity memory cards plus a portable hard disk give enough permanent offline storage.

hoq.questionText: A computer has 4 GB of RAM and a 500 GB hard disk. When a program is closed and the computer is shut down, why do unsaved changes disappear while saved files remain?

options.text: Because the hard disk is volatile and RAM is non-volatile
Because RAM is volatile while the hard disk is non-volatile
Because both RAM and the hard disk lose data at shutdown
Because the program deletes all files when it closes

hoq.explanation: Unsaved work sits in volatile RAM and is lost at shutdown, while saved files are written to the non-volatile hard disk and remain.

hoq.questionText: A school must back up 2 TB of student records every day, keep the data for years, and allow staff in different branches to view it. Which combination best meets all these needs?

options.text: Several flash disks shared by hand between branches
Only the RAM of the main school computer
Large hard disks for local backup together with cloud storage for sharing
A collection of CDs stored in one office

hoq.explanation: Large hard disks give reliable high-capacity local backups while cloud storage allows long-term keeping and access from different branches.
